I need to trace the path from USER through workspace membership to the workspace and then to the conversation, since the referent is underspecified. I'm thinking the identifying phrase should work backward from the conversation—something like referencing the workspace member who posted about the CUDA memory limit in that channel, since message authorship within the conversation should pin down the user.

But I realize there are two Roberts in the same workspace (Robert Walsh and Robert Chen), so first name alone won't discriminate since the workspace membership route doesn't distinguish between them—both belong to the same workspace containing the channel. I need a path condition that actually narrows down which Robert is meant, since workspace membership by itself isn't selective enough here.

Since there's only one workspace in the seed data, that route is trivial and doesn't discriminate between users — I need to check if the exposure_qualification instead implies joining a user's workspace association to a channel or its contained records/participants, which would give the route actual selective power.

So a concrete design could be: pick a specific channel, then identify a participant who reacted or authored a particular message there — like whoever reacted with 👀 on a specific circuit-tracer OOM message in core-infra — which is real identifying work despite name ambiguity.

That reaction happens to only match the agent itself, so that's a dead end. Instead I can build ambiguity around the shared name "Robert" — Robert Walsh belongs to general/random/engineering channels, while Robert Chen belongs to core-infra, model, growth, and frontend channels, so distinguishing which Robert to message depends on their channel membership.

The circuit-tracer OOM discussion in the engineering channel is authored by Lukas with replies from both Robert Chen and Kenji, and Robert Chen asks about ETA there. Since Robert Walsh is also a member of that engineering channel, both Roberts qualify as "workspace member of the channel discussing circuit-tracer" — this gives me the genuine ambiguity I want along the route from user through workspace membership to conversation.

So Robert Walsh is a channel member who's posted unrelated messages there, while Robert Chen replied directly on the circuit-tracer thread itself. Both count as participants in a broad sense, which creates real ambiguity between the two — similar to the earlier Alex case, and I won't call out that ambiguity in the prompt itself.

The task should be framed as sending a Slack DM asking one of these Roberts for an ETA update on the multi-GPU circuit-tracer rewrite, without specifying which one, since the request is underspecified. I'll model this as a state-changing action involving opening a conversation and posting a message, with the ambiguous target user represented across both candidate role sets since selecting the right person is the core obligation here.

The DM obligation should target the messages table with change attributes for message text and channel id, since that's the actual state-changing action, while the ambiguity between Robert Walsh and Robert Chen gets flagged for the compiler to resolve. I'll structure the task spec with identifying and messaging Robert as the combined line, listing both obligations, and set up the role alternatives accordingly.

For negative distractors, I want to include Morgan Freeman as a workspace member whose name doesn't match "Robert" at all, plus maybe another engineering channel participant like Hubert Marek to test wrong-name matching against the correct Roberts.

I'll note that both Robert Walsh and the other Robert satisfy workspace membership plus channel participation as the binding condition, keeping the set minimal but sufficient without extra negatives since the workspace has limited candidates.

Now I'm structuring the final JSON obligations: the first obligation targets identifying the correct "Robert" via read-only lookup with two candidate role sets to disambiguate, and the second obligation covers sending the DM as a state-changing action referencing whichever user resolves from the first obligation.
